chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abi Basir, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):
Regarding the divorced woman, she observes her waiting period (iddah) in her house, and she displays her adornment to him, 'Perhaps Allah will bring about some matter after that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a divorced woman's waiting period (iddah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam elaborates on the conduct of a divorced woman during her iddah, emphasizing the domestic sphere as a space for potential reconciliation. It highlights the psychological and social dimension of the waiting period, where the wife's display of adornment serves as a subtle invitation for the husband to reconsider the divorce, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the marital bond where possible.
